meta.description: Factors measured inside a small square footprint centred on each site, for the candidate sites of analogs.json, two more candidate sites proposed by a team member, and nine already-known analogs for comparison. Every value carries its scale: site, volcano or grid. kind 'known' means an already-known analog, not a new finding. footprintStatus 'provisional' means a team member should check the footprint.

methods.terrain: Copernicus DEM GLO-30, water pixels left out with the product's water body mask. Same function as earth.json (pipeline/terrain_metrics.py): mean Horn 3x3 slope, standard deviation of elevation. slope/roughness on 463 m posts, slopeFine/roughnessFine on 1 arc-second (about 31 m) posts.
methods.vegetation: Sentinel-2 L2A, 2025, up to 3 least-cloudy scenes per month (scene cloud cover under 80%). Per 10 m pixel: NDVI from bands 4 and 8 for observations classed vegetation, not vegetated, water or unclassified (open water is removed with the Copernicus DEM water body mask instead, because the classification labels dark lava as water); mean per month, then mean of months. ndvi is the footprint mean. Only scenes flagged as offset-corrected in the archive are used. bareFrac is the share of non-water pixels below 0.2.
methods.rock: Finest regional geologic map unit at the site coordinates from Macrostrat (large, medium or small scale maps only). If there is none, the volcano's major rock type from the Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program. If there is neither, a rock type stated in the abstract of a paper about the feature. Otherwise null.
methods.minerals: NASA EMIT L2B mineral identification, 60 m. Per site, the least cloudy granule (of at most 6 tried) in which the footprint is wholly inside the scene and at least 50% of its pixels are free of cloud, cirrus and water in the EMIT L2A mask. One date, nothing merged. Null where no granule qualifies.
methods.climate: Copied from the site's 0.5 degree cell in earth.json (scale: grid).

sites.name: Salar de Uyuni salt flat, Bolivia
sites.footprintNote: One 5 km sample of the salt flat.
sites.footprintBasis: 5 km sample of the salt surface at a single published point.
sites.coordinateSource: Wikidata Q76122 (Salar de Uyuni), coordinate statement, read 2026-11-15. One point on a salt flat of about 10,000 km2.
sites.caveat: The Copernicus DEM water body mask classes 96% of this footprint as water (the salt flat floods in the wet season) and Sentinel-2 classes most clear views of the salt as snow. Terrain on 463 m posts is therefore null, and slopeFine, roughnessFine, ndvi and bareFrac rest on the 4% of the footprint outside the mask. waterFrac here is not a measurement of open water.
